subject: Can I fit a local model with inla?

messages.author: 82a29501c95feac5
messages.subject: Can I fit a local model with inla?
parts:
Hi all, I want to use INLA+SPDE for spatial modeling. I want to know whether can I fit a local spatial model using INLA+SPDE  just like geographically weighted regression (GWR)? Or in particular, can I specify coefficients varying with spatial locations in INLA? Thank you.

Best regards,
Kuan

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I fit a local model with inla?

you can do similar to GWR, right. the SPDE approach is model-based,

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: Can I fit a local model with inla?
parts: What you are after is a Spatially Varying Coefficient (SVC) model. These can be analyzed in INLA using both aerial data and models (CAR) and continuous data and models (SPDE). Essentially, this is a random slope model where the random slope parameter is modeled with spatial structure. Looks like you want to do it using SPDE. The only tricky part is setting up the data stacks. Maybe you can do a bit of reading on SVC models and then I can help you code it in INLA?
